NKE.rationale: NKE presents a deeply unattractive fundamental picture across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Revenue is flat ($11.28B Q3, +0.1% YoY), earnings have collapsed (-35% YoY EPS, -34.5% net income), operating margin compressed from 7.5% to 5.8%, and operating cash flow cratered -76% YoY. ROE has halved from 32.2% to 16.0%. The Q4 FY2026 results (reported 2026-07-01) show the first underlying EPS growth in two years ($0.20 ex-tariff vs $0.14 prior year), but this is a marginal recovery from a deeply depressed base, and the $0.72 headline EPS is inflated by a non-recurring $986M tariff recovery. Greater China remains in structural decline (-12% reported, -17% currency-neutral). Pillar 2 (valuation): Trailing P/E of 28x on declining earnings is not cheap — it embeds a recovery assumption the numbers do not yet support. Earnings yield of 3.5% sits well below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.54%. P/B at compressed to 4.5x near trough, reflects the earnings collapse, a re-rating.. Pillar 3 (catalyst): Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for continued low-to mid-single-digit revenue decline. The tariff headwind (~$1.5B annually) and the tariff China in structural decline create persistent margin drag. The Dow removal risk adds passive selling pressure. The only near-term positive — wholesale recovery and running share gains — is insufficient to offset the magnitude of the earnings deterioration and the absence of a clear margin stabilization timeline. The risk-reward is asymmetric: limited upside if recovery materializes (already partly priced at 28x), significant further downside if deterioration continues toward $18-26 on normalized multiples.
